title: Finance & Legal: Procurement, Contract Approval, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard procedures for: budgeting & forecasting alignment, procurement and purchase approvals, contract intake and legal review, and revenue recognition & billing policies. It is intended for finance, procurement requesters, legal, and business owners who enter into commercial agreements or commit company spend.

Scope

- Applies to all purchases, vendor contracts, software licenses, and customer-facing commercial agreements where Redwood is the seller or buyer.
- Excludes petty cash purchases < $250 (follow AP petty cash guidelines) and previously executed enterprise Master Services Agreements (MSAs) that include specific delegated approval limits.

Key Principles

1. Spend must be budgeted or have an approved forecast variance exception before signature.
2. Contracts that create revenue or liability require Legal and Finance sign-off per the approval matrix below.
3. Use standard Redwood templates (SaaS SOW, Procurement PO, MSA, NDA) where possible to reduce legal review cycles.

Roles & Ownership

- Requester: Business owner initiating procurement or contract. Responsible for collecting requirements and drafting the initial request.
- Finance (FP&A): Validates budget/forecast alignment and cost-center charging.
- Procurement: Executes vendor onboarding questionnaires, PO issuance, and vendor setup in the AP system.
- Legal: Reviews contract risk, negotiates non-standard terms, and approves final signature-ready agreements.
- Contract Approver: Individual with authority per the approval matrix (typically Director+ for material commitments).
- Sales Ops (for customer contracts): Coordinates commercial terms and billing setup.

Budgeting and Forecasting Tie-ins

- All purchase requests must reference a budget line or a forecast ID. For requests outside of approved budget, attach a Forecast Exception Form and approval from the relevant VP of Product or Engineering.
- Quarterly forecast refresh: FP&A publishes updated forecast targets and a list of pre-approved vendor categories. Procurement will reject requests that materially exceed forecasts (>10% of department quarterly spend) without VP approval.

Procurement & Approval Matrix

Use the following approval matrix for both purchase commitments and contract signature. The matrix applies to combined multi-year commitments (total TCV) and one-time capital expenditures.

| Threshold (USD) | Required Approver(s) | Procurement/Legal Steps | Additional Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| < $5,000 | Requester/Manager | PR submitted in Procurement Portal; no PO if paid by corporate card | Budget check in portal |
| $5,000–$50,000 | Director of Requester + Finance FP&A reviewer | Procurement issues PO; Legal not required for standard SaaS/Reseller agreements | Vendor onboarding questionnaire if new vendor |
| $50,001–$250,000 | VP (or Head) + Finance Director + Procurement | Procurement issues PO; Legal review for non-standard terms; negotiation tracked in CLM | Business case and forecast impact required |
| $250,001–$1,000,000 | CFO + Legal Counsel + VP | Legal negotiates and approves; Procurement conducts security/compliance review; PO or MSA required | FP&A to confirm capital vs operating treatment |
| > $1,000,000 | CEO + CFO + Legal & Procurement execs | Executive steering approval; Board notification for multi-year material commitments | Detailed procurement RFP recommended |

Notes:
- All hardware purchases must include expected depreciation schedule for Finance.
- For capitalizable purchases, Finance must approve GL coding before PO issuance.

Contract Intake & Legal Review Process

1. Intake: Requester files a Contract Intake Form in the contracts portal (include SOW, commercial summary, budget/forecast reference, and requested countersignatory).
2. Triage: Legal classifies risk (Low / Medium / High) using the Risk Questionnaire. Low-risk (standard SaaS, NDAs) use playbook clauses and accelerated review SLA (48 business hours).
3. Negotiation: Legal negotiates non-standard terms; Requester retains responsibility for commercial trade-offs. Track redlines in CLM (Contract Lifecycle Management tool: Concordia).
4. Signature: Use designated signature authority table in the portal. Legal attaches executed contract to the CLM and notifies Procurement for vendor setup.
5. Post-signature: Contracts requiring ongoing obligations (support SLAs, data residency, or indemnity) must have an assigned contract owner and be added to the monthly contract review feed.

Standard Clause Guidance (High-level)

- NDAs: Use Redwood standard NDA. Approve exceptions only for specific legal reasons.
- Data processing & privacy: Add DPA for vendors processing customer data. Legal and Security must sign off on any cross-border data transfers.
- Indemnity & limitation of liability: Follow Legal's playbook caps based on revenue and contract type.
- Consumer-facing terms: Coordinate with Product and Security for compliance.

Contract Approval Workflow (numbered steps)

1. Create Contract Intake in portal and attach supporting docs.
2. Obtain budget confirmation from FP&A. If outside budget, attach Forecast Exception Form and VP approval.
3. Procurement runs vendor onboarding and security questionnaire for new vendors.
4. Legal triages and performs risk review; Legal returns to Requester with negotiation items.
5. Commercial and legal negotiate until terms are acceptable.
6. Obtain signature per signature authority table.
7. Procurement issues PO (if buyer) or Sales Ops configures billing (if Redwood is seller).
8. Upload executed agreement to CLM and assign contract owner.

Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy (summary)

This section summarizes Redwood's revenue recognition rules for the most common contract types. Detailed accounting treatment is maintained by Finance/RevRec and aligns with ASC 606 principles.

General rules:
- Revenue is recognized when control of promised goods or services is transferred to the customer in an amount that reflects the consideration Redwood expects to receive.
- For subscription-based SaaS: Recognize ratably over the subscription term starting on contractually agreed start date or activation date, whichever provides evidence of transfer of control.
- For usage-based billing: Recognize revenue in the period usage occurs (metered). Invoices may be lagged; revenue recognized when metered measurement is complete and collectability is probable.
- For professional services / implementation SOWs: Evaluate whether services are distinct or form a combined performance obligation. If distinct, recognize based on delivery milestones or percentage-of-completion where measurably reliable.
- Deferred revenue: Cash received before performance is a liability. Finance posts deferred revenue and recognizes on schedule.

Invoicing & Billing Setup:
- Sales Ops is responsible for billing setup in Stripe/Billing system. Billing cadence (monthly/annual/one-time) must be set prior to go-live.
- For prepaid annual contracts, create journal entries to defer revenue and amortize monthly.
- For multi-element arrangements (SaaS + professional services), Sales Ops flags in CLM and Finance applies contract-level revenue allocation.

Credit & Collections:
- Standard payment terms are Net 30 unless otherwise negotiated. Requests for extended terms must be approved by Finance Director.
- For past-due accounts, Collections follows the collections playbook with tiered escalation (30/60/90 days) and potential hold on service at 60+ days.

Audit & Controls

- All executed contracts and supporting procurement documents must be stored in CLM and Procurement Portal.
- Finance will perform quarterly sample audits to validate revenue recognition and PO-to-invoice matching.
- Segregation of duties: Requesters cannot approve their own POs beyond their manager level.

Exceptions & Escalations

- For non-standard legal terms that materially increase risk (data residency exceptions, open-ended indemnities, equity-based compensation), Legal will escalate to the GC and CFO with a recommended mitigation plan.
- For budget exceptions >10% of quarterly spend, FP&A routes to the relevant VP and CFO for approval.

Templates & Checklists

- Procurement Request Template (Procurement Portal)
- Contract Intake Form (CLM)
- Forecast Exception Form (Finance wiki)
- Standard NDA, SaaS MSA, Professional Services SOW templates (Legal repository)
